title: NeuroSelect-FS: A Feasibility Study for Multimodal Plasticity- and Context-Based Selection of Treatment Modalities in Treatment-Resistant Depression
summary:
NeuroSelect-FS
Summary:
This observational study investigates whether measurements of brain modifiability, as well as stress, sleep, activity, and living environment, can help in the future to better select appropriate treatment strategies for treatment-resistant depression. Clinical treatment with esketamine or rTMS is determined independently of the study and is not affected by participation.
NeuroSelect-tFS
Summary:
This technical pilot study with healthy adults examines whether the planned measurement methods function reliably and are suitable for everyday use. These methods include brief smartphone surveys, wearing a fitness tracker, questionnaires on stress and living environment, and two measurements of brain response to visual stimuli. The results serve solely to prepare for the subsequent patient study.
conditions: Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode severe without psychotic symptoms

interventions.name: NeuroSelect-FS is a prospective, monocentric, longitudinal, observational feasibility study in patients with treatment-resistant unipolar major depressive disorder. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Current unipolar major depressive disorder.
• Current moderate to severe depressive episode.
• Treatment-resistant depression, defined as non-response to at least two different     antidepressant treatments in the current episode.
• Clinical indication for esketamine or rTMS embedded in TAU.
• Stable antidepressant pharmacotherapy with an SSRI or SNRI for at least six weeks prior to study inclusion.
• Medication intended to remain unchanged until W6 unless clinical circumstances require modification.
• Sufficient German language skills.
• Internet access and compatible smartphone for EMA.
• Ability and willingness to wear a study-provided wearable device from W-2 to W6.
• Willingness and ability to complete twice-daily EMA during the two EMA assessment phases, from W-2 to W1 and from W4 to W6.
• Written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
• Bipolar disorder.
• Primary psychotic disorder or psychotic symptoms requiring alternative primary treatment.
• Neurological or severe medical condition interfering with study participation or data quality.
• Epilepsy or history of seizures.
• Known photosensitivity or contraindication to repeated visual stimulation.
• Brain tumor or relevant structural brain disease.
• Severe visual impairment not sufficiently corrected by glasses or contact lenses.
• Contraindications to clinically indicated esketamine or rTMS.
• Substance use disorder likely to interfere with participation.
• Inability to comply with study procedures.
• Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
